title: Reliance's Big Leap: Making Super-Strong, Lightweight Materials in India
description: Reliance Industries is building a massive plant in Gujarat to produce 'carbon fibre'. Carbon fibre is a material that is incredibly strong, yet much lighter t.

faq.q: What is the capacity of Reliance's new carbon fibre plant?
faq.a: Reliance's plant in Hazira, Gujarat, is planned to have a capacity of 20,000 Metric Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA) of carbon fibre.

faq.q: Which raw material is used to make carbon fibre at this plant?
faq.a: The plant will primarily use 'acrylonitrile' (ACN) as the feedstock, which is the precursor material for carbon fibre production.

faq.q: When is the plant expected to start production?
faq.a: Reliance aims to commence acrylonitrile production in 2023 and complete the first phase of the carbon fibre plant in 2025, as per earlier announcements. The recent announcement in September 2026 confirmed the construction is underway.

faq.q: How strong is carbon fibre compared to steel?
faq.a: Carbon fibre is known to be five times stronger than steel and twice as stiff, while being significantly lighter.

faq.q: Will this plant help India export carbon fibre?
faq.a: Yes, by establishing large-scale domestic production, India could not only meet its own growing demand but also potentially become a significant exporter of carbon fibre, enhancing its position in the global advanced materials market.
